title: Input symbol in an extractor configuration
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $q$ be an optional extractor control state, and let $i\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $i\le |x|$. For any buffered Boolean word $a$, integer head position $z$, and output word, the extractor configuration with input head just past the first $i$ symbols reads the $i$-th symbol of $x$, or no symbol if $i=|x|$.
hypotheses_covered: q is an optional extractor control state
the output is a Boolean word
replaced:
In an extractor configuration at input position $i \le \abs{x}$, the symbol
under the input head is the $i$-th bit of $x$ when $i < \abs{x}$ and the blank
otherwise, regardless of the buffer contents.
